biological.citation: Anon. 2025 - ERV3-MLT1 provides cis-regulatory elements for human placental functioning and are commonly dysregulated in human-specific preeclampsia (PMID: 41188995)
biological.summary: An upstream MLT1(G1) ERV element acts as an enhancer for EPS8L1, shown by reporter assay and genome editing. EPS8L1 is expressed in progenitor cytotrophoblasts and syncytiotrophoblasts and is overexpressed in preeclampsia. A soluble form is detectable in maternal plasma from about 24 weeks. EPS8L1 knockout in trophoblasts is lethal in vitro, and overexpression alters trophoblast behaviors characteristic of preeclampsia.

biological.citation: Structural basis of PxxDY motif recognition in SH3 binding (PMID: 18644376)
biological.summary: NMR solution structure of the Eps8L1 SH3 domain bound to the CD3epsilon PPVPNPDYEPIR peptide. Eps8L1 SH3 recognizes a PxxDY motif rather than canonical PxxP. Ile531 and Arg512 (salt bridge to D7) and E496 (hydrogen bond to Y8) determine this specificity.

biological.citation: Reciprocal regulation of SH3 and SH2 domain binding via tyrosine phosphorylation of a common site in CD3epsilon (PMID: 17617578)
biological.summary: A phage display screen identified Eps8L1 as a preferred SH3 partner of the CD3epsilon proline-rich region, together with Nck1/2. Binding maps to the PxxDY motif and is abolished by phosphorylation of Y166. In Jurkat T cells, TCR ligation induces Eps8L1 binding to endogenous CD3epsilon, and Y166 phosphorylation causes loss of that binding.

biological.citation: The eps8 family of proteins links growth factor stimulation to actin reorganization generating functional redundancy in the Ras/Rac pathway (PMID: 14565974)
biological.summary: Eps8L1 interacts with Abi1 and Sos-1, activates the Rac-GEF activity of Sos-1, and binds actin in vivo. It localizes to PDGF-induced F-actin-rich ruffles. Expressing it in eps8-/- fibroblasts restores RTK-mediated actin remodeling, which indicates functional redundancy with Eps8 in the Ras/Rac pathway.

biological.citation: Comparative immunohistochemical analysis suggests a conserved role of EPS8L1 in epidermal and hair follicle barriers of mammals (PMID: 37889356)
biological.summary: EPS8L1 mRNA is co-expressed with filaggrin and loricrin in terminally differentiated human keratinocytes. The protein is found in the epidermal granular layer and the hair follicle inner root sheath across mammals, partly at cell membranes. The gene has been lost in birds, and the pattern suggests a role in skin barrier function.

biological.citation: Immunolocalization of Pglyrp3 and Eps8l1 proteins in the regenerating lizard epidermis indicates they contribute to epidermal barrier formation (PMID: 36854226)
biological.summary: Eps8l is accumulated in the wound epidermis and in the shedding layer of regenerating lizard tail scales. This suggests a possible role in epidermal barrier formation or regeneration, but its function remains unknown.

biological.citation: Gene expression profile associated with Asmt knockout-induced depression-like behaviors and exercise effects in mouse hypothalamus (PMID: 35771226)
biological.summary: Eps8l1 was one of the differentially expressed genes in the hypothalamus of Asmt knockout mice with depression-like behavior, and also after swimming exercise. The change was partly confirmed by qRT-PCR.

biological.citation: Effects of Tcte1 knockout on energy chain transportation and spermatogenesis: implications for male infertility (PMID: 38650655)
biological.summary: Eps8l1 is identified as Drc3, a component of the nexin-dynein regulatory complex (N-DRC), and was visualized by immunofluorescence in mouse sperm. In Tcte1-/- males, N-DRC components including Eps8l1 were not transported to the sperm flagella.
biological.sample_size: Mouse WT, Tcte1+/- and Tcte1-/- males; 248 infertile human males screened for TCTE1

biological.citation: Feature Genes in Neuroblastoma Distinguishing High-Risk and Non-high-Risk Neuroblastoma Patients: Development and Validation Combining Random Forest With Artificial Neural Network (PMID: 35911385)
biological.summary: EPS8L1 was selected by random forest as a feature differentially expressed gene distinguishing high-risk from non-high-risk neuroblastoma. It was part of a 5-gene model with high classification accuracy.
biological.sample_size: GSE49710 training set; GSE73517 validation set

biological.citation: Proteomics and Metabolic Characteristics of Boar Seminal Plasma Extracellular Vesicles Reveal Biomarker Candidates Related to Sperm Motility (PMID: 39067049)
biological.summary: EPS8L1 was one of seven differentially expressed proteins in boar seminal plasma extracellular vesicles between high and low sperm motility groups. This marks it as a candidate biomarker of sperm motility.
